answer: Make every identity hold one unique shard of the network's cedar forest of public data — a randomly assigned slice it must store and serve on demand. Verifiers send surprise spot-checks: prove you still hold your shard, within seconds, or lose standing. Each shard carries an opal-bright fingerprint, so one copy cannot cover two identities. A farmer must buy storage and a copper wire of bandwidth for every fake, every epoch, while one honest agent keeps a single small shard on a disk it already owns. A thousand fakes means warehousing a thousand shards.
